podcast.title: Condition for Joining Fleetwood Mac (1975)
podcast.body: Upon being invited to fill the void left by Bob Welch in 1975, Lindsey Buckingham insisted that his girlfriend, Stevie Nicks, also be accepted into Fleetwood Mac as a condition of his own membership. "Lindsey Buckingham insisted that his girlfriend Stevie Nicks be accepted into what remained of Fleetwood Mac at that time when Lindsey Buckingham was invited to fill the void."

podcast.title: Controlling Nature in Relationship with Stevie Nicks
podcast.body: Lindsey Buckingham's "controlling nature" was cited as a primary factor in the permanent splintering of his "fractious relationship" with Stevie Nicks during the intense period of recording "Rumours." "done in by Lindsey's controlling nature and an affair Stevie had."

podcast.title: Criticism of Guitar Work on *Rumours*
podcast.body: Music critic Robert Hilburn criticized Buckingham's guitar work on the *Rumours* album as being "too muted," suggesting it contributed to the album's studio work being "too undemanding" compared to the band's more dynamic live performances. "Lindsey Buckingham's guitar work is too muted."

podcast.title: Exclusion of "Silver Springs" from Rumours
podcast.body: Lindsey Buckingham successfully lobbied to exclude Stevie Nicks' "incendiary and raw" composition "Silver Springs" from the "Rumours" LP, highlighting the deep personal tensions within Fleetwood Mac during its creation. "The B side of the Go Your Own Way single, the Stevie Nicks composition Silver Springs, was so incendiary and raw, Buckingham successfully lobbied to exclude it from the Rumors LP."

podcast.title: Involvement in Internal Love Triangle
podcast.body: He was a central figure in a "messy love triangle" with Stevie Nicks and Mick Fleetwood, which, alongside other internal dramas and drug use, provided significant material for the band's songwriting, particularly on *Rumours*. "relationship drama Stevie and Mick and Stevie and Lindsey form a messy love triangle."

podcast.title: Modifying Voice for Big Love
podcast.body: On the song "Big Love" from "Tango in the Night," Lindsey Buckingham modified his own voice to achieve a female vocal sound for backing parts. "even Lindsey himself, modifying his own voice to sound female."

podcast.title: Outsized Personality - Joining Fleetwood Mac
podcast.body: Lindsey Buckingham, along with Stevie Nicks, possessed an "outsized personality" that contributed to Fleetwood Mac's transformation into multi-platinum superstars when they joined in the mid-70s. He was a guitarist and "studio whiz." "Vocalist Stevie Nicks, and guitarist and studio whiz Lindsey Buckingham."

podcast.title: Package Deal Requirement - Joining Fleetwood Mac
podcast.body: When Mick Fleetwood offered Lindsey Buckingham the lead guitarist job for Fleetwood Mac in late 1974, Buckingham insisted that he and Stevie Nicks were a "package deal," meaning both had to be hired. Fleetwood agreed, leading to the pivotal transformation of the band. "Buckingham insisted that he and Nix were a package deal so Fleetwood agreed to hire Stevie as well."

podcast.title: Pre-Fleetwood Mac Performance - Fritz
podcast.body: Lindsey Buckingham had been performing with Stevie Nicks since the late 1960s, with Nicks singing lead in his psychedelic rock band called Fritz. This early collaboration established their musical partnership before they formed Buckingham Nicks and later joined Fleetwood Mac. "Buckingham and Nix have been performing with each other since the late 60s when Lindsay got Stevie to sing lead with his psychedelic rock band Fritz."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Romantic and Musical Partners - Buckingham Nicks Duo
podcast.body: Before joining Fleetwood Mac, Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks were both romantic and musical partners, performing together since the late 60s and releasing the album *Buckingham Nicks* in 1973. Their relationship dynamics would later become a significant part of Fleetwood Mac's drama. "Now a romantic couple as well as musical partners, the duo recorded Buckingham Nix with the cream of LA session players."

podcast.title: Writing and Harmonizing with Christine McVie - New Era
podcast.body: Upon joining Fleetwood Mac, Lindsey Buckingham quickly began writing and harmonizing with Christine McVie, who had already adapted her songwriting to the "LA rock ethos." Their collaboration produced tracks like "World Turning," a hard-driving country rock staple. "Lindsay Buckingham not only contributed a couple of songs of his own, he quickly began writing and harmonizing with Christine McVe, who again had already refashioned her songwriting around the LA rock ethos."
